title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text: These questions follow the order of Chapter 5. Each of the first eight groups checks one or two sections of the chapter, and the last group reviews the whole chapter. The “Self-check” buttons in the chapter lead to these groups. Nothing you answer is recorded.

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
section: What a Class Model Adds and Where It Starts
text:
What a Class Model Adds and Where It Starts
Read the sections

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A use case diagram for a plant’s maintenance records draws a figure for each actor. Which label is right for one of those figures?



Maintenance planner

Yes. Users are named by role, not by person, and a role that uses the system is an actor.



The name of the planner who works the day shift

A person may leave or change jobs, and several people may share a role. The diagram names the role.



Schedule a repair

That is a use case, drawn as an oval inside the system’s boundary, not an actor.



The maintenance database

The system is the box that marks the boundary. An actor is outside it and uses it.



Check Show answer Reset



2. A plant’s maintenance group is writing the documents for a new database of machine repairs. Which statement about these documents is correct?



A use case is a statement precise enough to test, beginning “the system shall”

That is a requirement. A use case is a function of the system as one of its users sees it, a sequence of steps the user starts to get something done.



The problem statement lists every actor and the use cases each one starts

That is the work of the use case diagram. The problem statement is a short narrative of why the system is needed, its setting, and what it must do.



A sentence saying that the system does not schedule technicians belongs in the problem statement

Yes. Saying what the system will not do draws its boundary, and a boundary left undrawn grows during design.



“Reports must appear within two seconds” is a use case

It is a requirement about a quality rather than a function, a nonfunctional requirement.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Classes and Attributes
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. Which names follow the naming conventions of UML that the book’s class models use? Select every one that does.
Select all that apply.



CustomerOrder, as the name of a class

Yes. A class name is a singular noun with each word capitalized.



requestedShipDate, as the name of an attribute

Yes. An attribute name begins in lower case, and each later word is capitalized.



Customers, as the name of a class

A class describes one object, so its name is singular: Customer.



customer_order, as the name of a class

Lower case with underscores is how the book names tables and columns. A class name is written CustomerOrder.



Check Show answer Reset



2. Two customers of a class model have the same name, the same city, and the same state, and every other fact recorded about them is the same too. What are they?



One object, since nothing recorded tells them apart

Objects are not told apart by their facts alone.



Two objects, since an object has an identity of its own

Yes. Two objects remain two even when every recorded fact about them is the same. How the database keeps them apart is decided when the model becomes tables.



A mistake in the class model, which must be repaired by splitting Customer into two classes

Both are customers, with the same kinds of facts, so they belong to one class.



Two classes that happen to share their attributes

Both are customers. They are two members of the one class Customer.



Check Show answer Reset



3. A gauge record keeps its calibration lab’s address as one attribute, “14 Oak St., Tulsa, OK 74103”. The quality department now asks for the gauges calibrated by labs in each state. Which modeling choice does the request call for?



Keep the address as one attribute, since it is printed whole on the certificate

Printing it whole is one use, but the new request needs one part of it on its own. A query would have to pick the state out of the text, and an address typed another way would slip past it.



Split the address into attributes, at least so that the state is one of them

Yes. The test is whether any query, rule, or sort needs part of the value on its own. The state is now needed alone, so it becomes an attribute with a domain of its own.



Record two attributes, address1 and address2

Numbered attributes form a repeating group; they do not separate the state from the rest.



The value is not atomic because it contains commas, so it must become a class

Whether a value is atomic depends on its domain and how the business uses it, not on how it looks.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Associations and Multiplicity
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A class model draws WorkCenter 1 -- 0..* Machine. Which sentence reads the 0..* correctly?



Each machine stands in zero or more work centers

This reads the number from the wrong end. The 0..* is written at the Machine end, so it is a count of machines.



Each work center has zero or more machines

Yes. The 0..* is written at the Machine end and counts the machines of one work center. The other sentence, from the 1, is that each machine stands in exactly one work center.



Each work center has at least one machine

A minimum of 0 means a work center may have no machines.



There are zero or more work centers in the plant

The 0..* says nothing about how many work centers the plant has.



Check Show answer Reset



2. Riverside Hardware placed order SO-5001. In the terms of a class model, what is this fact?



A link, one member of the association between customers and their orders

Yes. Links are to an association what objects are to a class: its members.



An attribute of Customer

An order is an object of its own, with facts of its own. The connection between the two is drawn as an association.



A multiplicity

A multiplicity is written at an end of an association and counts objects. This fact is one connection, not a count.



A class

A class describes many objects. This fact concerns one customer and one order.



Check Show answer Reset



3. An association Truck 0..1 -- 0..* Delivery connects trucks and deliveries. What does the minimum of 0 at the Truck end allow?



A truck to exist with no deliveries

That is the minimum at the Delivery end, which counts the deliveries of one truck.



A delivery to exist that is not yet assigned to any truck

Yes. The minimum at an end decides whether an object at the other end may exist without a link. Here a delivery may have no truck.



A delivery to be made by several trucks

The maximum at the Truck end is 1, so a delivery has at most one truck.



Nothing; the minimum matters only after the model becomes tables

The minimum is a rule of the business in the model. Mapped to tables, a minimum of 1 would become a foreign key declared NOT NULL.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Association Classes and Qualified Associations
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. At stage D4, StockLevel is drawn as an association class on the association Warehouse 0..* -- 0..* Product, joined to its line by a dashed line. Which statements about it are correct? Select every one that is.
Select all that apply.



Each link between a warehouse and a product has exactly one StockLevel object

Yes. The association class is the association seen as a class, so its objects and the links correspond one to one.



A StockLevel object cannot exist without its link

Yes. A stock level is the link between one warehouse and one product, with its quantity on hand and reorder point.



The dashed line needs a multiplicity at each of its ends

An association class has no multiplicity of its own. The multiplicities are those of the association it is attached to.



StockLevel also needs a line to Warehouse and a line to Product

Lines of its own would make StockLevel an ordinary class, a different model. The association class already belongs to the association between the two.



Check Show answer Reset



2. The cloud instance diagram of the bill of materials draws one cloud for parts in the role of assembly and one for parts in the role of component. The wheel assembly WA-10 appears as a dot in both clouds. What does that mean?



The database holds two parts numbered WA-10

A part number names one part. The two dots are one part drawn twice.



WA-10 is one object playing two roles: an assembly of its own components, and a component of the HT-100

Yes. In a recursive association an object of the class can be linked to another of the same class. A cloud for each role keeps the lines readable, and the role names say which end of each link is which.



The diagram is wrong, since an object may appear in only one cloud

Drawing a cloud for each role is a choice made for readability. The role names tell the reader that both clouds hold parts.



WA-10 is both a manufactured part and a purchased part

Being an assembly and being a component are roles in the bill of materials, not subclasses of Part.



Check Show answer Reset



3. A hypothetical ternary association links operators, machines, and work orders, one link for each run, with 0..* at the WorkOrder end. What does that 0..* say?



Each work order is run by any number of operators

The multiplicity at an end of a ternary association counts the objects at that end, not at another end.



An operator may run a given machine on any number of work orders, including none

Yes. At an end of a ternary association, the multiplicity says how many objects at that end may be linked to a given pair of objects at the other two ends.



The plant has zero or more work orders

Multiplicity counts the objects linked to other objects, not the size of a class.



A work order may exist without any machine

The 0..* is a count of work orders for a given operator and machine; it says nothing about work orders on their own.



Check Show answer Reset



4. A class diagram shows a hollow diamond in the middle of the drawing, with a line from it to each of three classes. What does the diamond mark?



A ternary association, an association whose links each connect three objects

Yes. UML draws the association itself as the diamond, with a line to each class it relates.



An aggregation of three parts in one whole

The diamond of an aggregation sits at the end of a line, against the whole. This diamond stands alone, with three lines leaving it.



A composition of three classes

Composition is drawn with a filled diamond at the whole’s end of a line.



A generalization with three subclasses

Generalization is drawn with a hollow triangle at the superclass.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Aggregation and Composition
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. In a composition that is not recursive, the multiplicity at the whole’s end is 1. Why?



Because UML requires the number 1 next to every diamond

The number comes from what composition says about each part, not from a drawing rule.



Because each part belongs to exactly one whole and cannot exist without it

Yes. A minimum of 0 would let a part exist with no whole, and a maximum above 1 would let it belong to two.



Because a whole has exactly one part

The number at the whole’s end counts wholes for one part. A whole may have many parts, as an order has many lines.



Because the part’s table will have a primary key

A class model shows no keys. The multiplicity states a rule of the business.



Check Show answer Reset



2. True or False: UML defines aggregation precisely, so two modelers who follow UML will always draw the hollow diamond in the same places.



True

UML leaves the exact meaning of aggregation to the modeler. The book fixes its own use: a part that is part of the whole but has a life of its own.



False

Right. Because UML leaves aggregation’s meaning open, a model that uses it should say what it means by it. This book uses it for a part that can outlive its whole or move to another.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Generalization
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. UML names the opposite of {disjoint}. Which keyword allows an object to belong to more than one subclass?



{overlapping}

Yes. A part bought in one season and made in another would need {overlapping} in place of {disjoint}.



{incomplete}

That keyword is the opposite of {complete}, not of {disjoint}.



{ordered}

{ordered} marks an end of an association whose sequence matters. It has nothing to do with subclasses.



{shared}

UML gives no such keyword for generalization.



Check Show answer Reset



2. In a class diagram, the name of the superclass Part is written in italics. What does that say?



That Part is a role played in an association

A role is written as a role name at the end of an association, not as a class.



That Part is an abstract class, with no objects of its own

Yes. Every part belongs to some subclass, so Part has no objects apart from theirs. It still holds what the subclasses share.



That Part has been eliminated from the model

An eliminated candidate is not drawn at all.



That Part is a derived class, computed from its subclasses

Italics mark an abstract class. A derived attribute is one computed from others, which is a different idea.



Check Show answer Reset



3. In a cloud instance diagram, how are the objects of a subclass drawn?



In a separate cloud beside the superclass’s cloud, with a line from each object to its superclass object

A manufactured part is a part, one object, not two objects joined by a link.



As a cloud inside the superclass’s cloud, since a subclass’s objects are a subset of the superclass’s objects

Yes. Each manufactured part is also a part, so its dot lies inside the cloud of Part as well as inside the cloud of ManufacturedPart.



Only in the superclass’s cloud, since a subclass has no objects of its own

It is the superclass that may have no objects of its own. A subclass’s objects are the ones drawn in its cloud.



Generalization cannot be drawn in a cloud instance diagram

The diagram draws it naturally: a cloud inside a cloud.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
section: Building and Reviewing a Class Model
text:
Building and Reviewing a Class Model
Read the sections

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. An analyst describes a class HandTruckModel as “the HT-100 and the HT-200”. Which test of a class’s soundness does that description fail?



The more than a list test

Yes. A class defined only by listing its members is not yet understood. Its description should give the test that decides whether a new model, added next year, belongs.



The uniformity test

Uniformity asks whether every object of the class has the same kinds of facts and relationships. A list of two members says nothing either way.



The or test

The or test looks for a description that joins unlike things with “or”, which may hide two classes. This description joins two things of one kind.



None; listing the members is the clearest description a class can have

A list fixes today’s members but gives no rule for tomorrow’s, which is what a class description must supply.



Check Show answer Reset



2. A data dictionary holds an entry for each association of a class model as well as for each class and attribute. What does an association’s entry give? Select every one that it does.
Select all that apply.



The association’s name and the classes it relates

Yes. The entry begins by saying which association it describes, such as Shipment leaves from Warehouse.



The multiplicity at each end

Yes. Each end’s multiplicity is stated in words.



The reason for each multiplicity

Yes. A reason, such as a shipment being loaded at one dock, lets the business confirm the rule or correct it.



The foreign key column that will implement it

A class model leaves the implementation to the mapping into tables, so the data dictionary of the model names no columns.



Check Show answer Reset



3. A reviewer traces the request “which supplier delivered each lot of steel used on a work order” through a class model and finds no path of associations from WorkOrder to Supplier. What does the review conclude?



The request is answered by a join, so the model does not need a path

The joins of a query follow the model’s associations. A request with no path has nothing for the joins to follow.



The model is missing something the business needs, which is cheaper to repair now than after tables are loaded

Yes. A request with no path means the model is missing something. Whether to add it is then a decision for the business.



The request should be dropped, since the problem statement did not list it

The list of requests is part of what the business must review; a missing request is a gap in the documents, not a reason to ignore it.



A foreign key supplierFk should be added to WorkOrder

A class model shows relationships as associations, not as reference attributes.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Reading Other Notations
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. True or False: the marks of a crow’s foot diagram sit at the opposite ends of a line from where UML writes its multiplicities, so a reader must swap the ends when translating.



True

The marks sit at the same ends as UML’s numbers, so no swap is needed.



False

Right. Each end’s marks count the objects at that end, as a UML multiplicity does, so the rule for reading an association as two sentences applies unchanged.



Check Show answer Reset



2. A reader finds a data model in another book that draws each relationship as a diamond between the boxes it connects. What is it, and what does this book say about it?



A UML diagram full of aggregations, read as this chapter reads them

The diamond of an aggregation sits at the end of a line, against the whole, not between two boxes.



A crow’s foot diagram, read with the table of crow’s foot marks

Crow’s foot notation draws a relationship as a plain line with marks at its ends.



Peter Chen’s original entity-relationship notation, which this book does not use but which can be translated by the same method

Yes. Chen’s notation draws relationships as diamonds. A reader who meets it translates it construct by construct, as the book does for crow’s foot notation.



A notation that cannot express multiplicities, and so cannot be translated

The book’s point is the opposite: other notations say much the same things with different marks.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 5 Self-Checks
text:
Review of the Whole Chapter
Read the chapter summary

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. An analyst follows every step of the method for building a class model, from the candidate classes to the data dictionary, with care. The problem statement never mentions the weight of a shipment. What will the model say about weight?



It will include a weight, since step 4 asks what every object of a class has

Step 4 finds attributes in the documents and in what the business brings to the model. No step invents a fact that nobody mentioned.



Nothing, and no step of the method will notice that it is missing

Yes. The method finds only what the documents mention, which is why the documents, like the list of requests, are part of what the business must review.



It will record the weight as a derived attribute

A derived attribute is computed from facts that are recorded. Nothing recorded gives a weight.



The data dictionary will flag the gap

The data dictionary describes the names the model has. It cannot describe a fact that was never named.



Check Show answer Reset



2. True or False: the steps of the method for building a class model are done once each, in order, from finding the candidates to writing the data dictionary.



True

Later steps often send the analyst back to earlier ones.



False

Right. Eliminating a candidate often turns it into an attribute of another class, and finding an association often shows that its links carry facts, which adds an association class.



Check Show answer Reset



3. UML has its own picture of instances, the object diagram, which draws each object as a box. How does the book’s cloud instance diagram compare with it?



It shows multiplicities that an object diagram cannot

Neither picture writes multiplicities. Both draw particular objects and links, from which a multiplicity can be counted.



It says the same things, and its clouds make it hard to miss that a class is a set of objects

Yes. Every statement a class diagram makes is a statement about the members of sets, and the clouds draw the sets.



It replaces the class diagram, so a model needs no class diagram once its clouds are drawn

A cloud instance diagram shows a few objects at a moment. The class diagram states the rules every set of objects must follow.



It shows the keys of each object, which an object diagram leaves out

A cloud instance diagram labels each dot with a business identifier, such as a customer number; it shows no keys chosen for tables.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 10 Self-Checks
text: These questions follow the order of Chapter 10. Each of the first five groups checks one or two sections of the chapter, and the last group reviews the whole chapter. The “Self-check” buttons in the chapter lead to these groups. Nothing you answer is recorded.

title: Chapter 10 Self-Checks
section: A Program’s View of a Database
text:
A Program’s View of a Database
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A program that uses the KSL connects to the book’s PostgreSQL database with nothing else added to its build. What part of JDBC makes that possible?



The KSL includes PostgreSQL’s driver, the library that speaks PostgreSQL’s protocol

Yes. JDBC is a set of interfaces; each database system implements them with a driver, and the program needs the driver for the system it reaches.



JDBC itself speaks every database system’s protocol

JDBC is a standard set of interfaces. It is the driver, one per database system, that does the speaking.



The KSL starts a copy of the PostgreSQL server inside the program

PostgreSQL is a server of its own, always running. The program connects to it; it does not run it.



DataGrip must be open, since the program sends its SQL through DataGrip’s console

A program and DataGrip are separate clients of the same server. Each opens its own connection.



Check Show answer Reset



2. The column order_date is DATE. Which call reads it as a Kotlin LocalDate?



rows.getObject("order_date", LocalDate::class.java)

Yes. getObject, given the class to return, reads the date as a LocalDate, the Kotlin type that matches DATE.



rows.getString("order_date")

getString returns the date’s text, which the program would still have to turn into a date.



rows.getInt("order_date")

A date is not a whole number; getInt reads INTEGER columns.



rows.getBigDecimal("order_date")

getBigDecimal reads exact decimal numbers, the NUMERIC columns.



Check Show answer Reset



3. LotMeasurements reads its rows with while (rows.next()) { ... }. It is given a lot number that no inspection has, so the query returns no rows. What happens?



The loop body never runs, and the program prints only its heading

Yes. rows.next() moves to the next row and returns false when there is none, here on the first call.



The loop runs once, reading NULL for every column

A result set with no rows has no row to read; the first call of rows.next() returns false.



executeQuery() raises an error, since the lot does not exist

A query that matches no rows is not an error. It returns a result set with no rows.



The loop never ends, since rows.next() keeps waiting for a row

rows.next() does not wait; it returns false when the rows are used up.



Check Show answer Reset



4. The book writes every connection, prepared statement, and result set inside a use block. Which of these are reasons? Select every one that applies.
Select all that apply.



Each of the three holds resources on the database server until it is closed

Yes. Closing releases them.



use closes the object when its block ends, however the block ends, an exception included

Yes. A close written by hand at the end of the block is skipped when an exception leaves the block early.



A program that forgets to close them eventually exhausts the server’s connections

Yes. The failure shows up later, often far from the code that caused it.



use commits the transaction when the block ends

Committing is the connection’s commit(), or auto-commit. use only closes.



use makes the query run faster

use changes when an object is closed, not how the query runs.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 10 Self-Checks
text:
Parameterized Queries and SQL Injection
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A function pastes a lot number into its SQL text, "WHERE i.lot_number = '$lotNumber'", and counts the lot’s measurements. It is given the input L7005-03' OR '1'='1. What does it count?



The two measurements of lot L7005-03

The quote in the input ends the SQL string early, so the rest of the input is read as SQL.



Every measurement in the table

Yes. The condition becomes i.lot_number = 'L7005-03' OR '1'='1', which is true of every row. The input has changed what the query does.



Nothing, because no lot has that number

That is what a parameterized query counts. Pasted into the SQL, the input is not treated as a lot number.



The driver refuses the statement as a syntax error

The quotes in this input happen to balance, so the statement is valid SQL with a different meaning.



Check Show answer Reset



2. A lot number with a mistyped apostrophe, L7005'03, is given to a function that supplies it with setString. The function counts 0 measurements rather than failing. Why?



The driver strips the apostrophe and searches for L700503, which does not exist

Nothing is stripped. The value is compared exactly as given.



The value never becomes part of the SQL text, so the apostrophe is only a character in a lot number that no lot has

Yes. The statement was parsed before the value arrived, so no character in the value can end a string or start new SQL.



The database recognizes the apostrophe as an attack and returns no rows

The database recognizes nothing. It simply uses the value as a value.



A parameterized query skips any value that contains a quote

It does not skip the value. A customer named with an apostrophe is found by the same query.



Check Show answer Reset



3. A function counts the measurements of the lots inspected between two dates that a user types. Which way of writing it follows the chapter’s rule?



SQL text built from constants, with a ? for each date, and each date supplied with a setter such as setObject

Yes. A value that comes from outside the program goes into SQL only as a parameter.



SQL text built with a string template, after checking that each input looks like a date

A check of the input is not the rule, and a check can miss a case. The value still becomes part of the SQL text.



SQL text built with a string template, since a date contains no quotes

The input is whatever the user typed; nothing makes it a date until the program treats it as a value.



SQL text built with each date’s quotes doubled by the program

Doubling quotes by hand is the repair a parameter makes unnecessary, and the value is still part of the SQL text.



Check Show answer Reset



4. True or False: A prepared statement prevents SQL injection by examining each value for dangerous characters, such as quotes, before sending it.



True

Nothing in the value is examined. The protection comes from when the value arrives, not from what it contains.



False

Right. The SQL, with its ?, reaches the database first and is parsed; the values follow separately, and the database uses each as a value, never as SQL, whatever characters it contains.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 10 Self-Checks
section: CRUD and the Data Access Object
text:
CRUD and the Data Access Object
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A program records inspections, reports on them, and corrects them, and its SQL is written wherever it is needed. What does moving that SQL into a data access object change?



The tables move out of the database into the program

The tables stay in the database. Only the place where the program’s SQL is written changes.



All of the SQL for inspections sits in one class, which the rest of the program calls by methods named for what they do

Yes. A change to the tables is made in one class, and the rest of the program reads as the business does.



The program no longer needs SQL, since the DAO generates it

The DAO is written by hand, with SQL in each of its methods. It gathers the SQL; it does not generate it.



Each data class learns to save itself to the database

The data classes know nothing about databases. Only the DAO sends SQL.



Check Show answer Reset



2. The data class Inspection names its part by partNumber and has no property for part_fk or inspection_pk. Where do those keys come from when an inspection is stored?



The program looks them up before calling the DAO

Then every caller would handle surrogate keys, which is what the DAO exists to hide.



The DAO looks up part_pk by the part number, and the database generates inspection_pk

Yes. Translating business keys into surrogate keys is the DAO’s real work, done at run time every time an object is stored.



The data class computes them from the part number

A data class only holds values. It cannot know the keys the database assigned.



They are not needed, since quality.inspection has no foreign keys

The inspection refers to its part and its operator by foreign keys, which must be filled.



Check Show answer Reset



3. The DAO’s create is given a gauge file whose second characteristic is spelled Lenght. The inspection and the diameter insert without error; the length’s insert fails. What is in the database afterward?



The inspection and the diameter

That is the half a lot the transaction exists to prevent.



The inspection alone

The diameter’s insert succeeded before the failure, so it was in the same position as the inspection’s.



Nothing from that file

Yes. The catch rolls back everything the method did, so the file records all or none.



All three rows, the length with a NULL characteristic

The NOT NULL foreign key refused the length’s row, and the rollback then removed the rest.



Check Show answer Reset



4. In the UML diagrams of the pattern, what does a dashed arrow from the program to the data access object say?



The program uses the DAO, calling its operations, without holding a lasting link to it

Yes. A dashed arrow is a dependency. A solid arrow is an association, a link the object keeps.



The DAO is a subclass of the program

Nothing in the diagram is a subclass; the arrow shows use.



The DAO keeps a link to the program for its whole lifetime

A lasting link is an association, drawn solid, like the DAO’s arrow to its Connection.



The program sends SQL to the database through the arrow

Only the DAO sends SQL. The program depends on the DAO, never on the database.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 10 Self-Checks
text:
The KSL Database Utilities
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A program sets the default schema and then counts a table’s rows:
db.defaultSchemaName = "production"
println(db.numRows("measurement"))
measurement is in the quality schema. What happens?



It prints the number of rows of quality.measurement

A method given a table name alone looks only in the default schema.



It stops with an error that the table does not exist

Finding no table in the default schema is not an error here.



It prints 0, and the KSL only logs a warning

Yes. A wrong count that looks like an answer is the risk, so set defaultSchemaName to the schema you work in, or name the schema.



It searches every schema and counts the first measurement it finds

Only the default schema is searched.



Check Show answer Reset



2. A data class extends DbTableData to give one table CRUD without SQL. Which statements about it are true? Select every one that applies.
Select all that apply.



Its properties are named as the table’s columns

Yes. The KSL writes each property to the column of the same name.



Its properties are in the columns’ order

Yes. The KSL reads a row into the properties by position.



After insertDbDataIntoTable, a generated key is set in the object

Yes. The key the database chose is copied back, so a later update can find the row.



It can record an inspection and its measurements in one transaction

It is limited to what one table can do. Work across tables in one transaction needs a DAO.



It looks up foreign keys from business keys held in other tables

It knows nothing of business keys in other tables; that is the hand-written DAO’s work.



Check Show answer Reset



3. DatabaseIfc.toDataFrame turns a result set into a data frame. A Statistic needs Double values, and the measured_value column is NUMERIC(10,4). Why does the program convert each value with (it as Number).toDouble()?



The data frame holds every column as text

The frame’s columns are typed. A NUMERIC column has the type BigDecimal.



The frame holds the values as BigDecimal, so a cast as Double fails, while Number covers whichever numeric type the column holds

Yes. Number covers whichever numeric type the column holds, and toDouble() gives each value the type Statistic takes.



toDouble() rounds each value to four decimal places

The conversion does not round; it changes the type.



Without it, Statistic would count each value twice

The conversion concerns the values’ type, not how many there are.



Check Show answer Reset

The program sets a row’s parameters and adds it with addBatch(), then sends all rows with executeBatch()

Yes. That is the sequence of a batch.



The rows travel to the server together, rather than one statement and one wait per row

Yes. That is the reason to batch.



executeBatch() is called once for each row, after its addBatch()

JDBC, with the SQL written as a string

jOOQ without generated classes, naming columns in strings

jOOQ with its code generator, which writes a typed field for every column

Yes. The column becomes a generated name, and a misspelled one does not compile.



Any approach, since PostgreSQL checks the SQL when the program is compiled

1. The hand calculation says a work center should be busy about 80 percent of the time. The simulation, over 30 replications, reports its utilization as 0.62. What is the right next step?



Report the simulated waiting times, since the simulation is more detailed than the hand calculation

A model whose utilization disagrees with its own inputs is not doing what those inputs say. Its waiting times cannot be trusted until the gap is explained.



Look for an error in the model or in the inputs it read, such as the wrong number of machines, before using any of its results

Yes. A utilization follows from the mean arrival rate, the mean time per lot, and the number of machines, so the simulation must agree with the hand value up to random variation. A gap this large points to a mistake.



Run more replications until the two values agree

Random variation over 30 replications accounts for differences in the second or third decimal place, not a gap of 0.18.



Replace the hand value with the simulated one, since hand calculations ignore randomness

The hand value already uses the mean of the random processing times. Randomness changes how long lots wait, not the fraction of time the work center is busy on average.

2. Two experiments of the frame line are run with the KSL’s resetStartStreamOption set, one with two welders and one with three. True or False: replication 7 of one experiment then sees the same arrivals and the same processing-time variations as replication 7 of the other.



True

Correct. This is common random numbers: each experiment starts from the same random numbers, so the scenarios differ only in what differs between them, here the number of welders.



False

Setting the option makes each experiment start from the same random numbers. Replications within one experiment still differ from each other; it is the replications with the same number in the two experiments that match.

1. The KSL stores its model elements as a nested set, with a left_count and a right_count for each. In a self-join of model_element to itself, aliased parent and child, which condition on the numbers finds every element below a given parent, at any depth?



child.left_count = parent.left_count + 1

This finds at most the first element the walk reaches after the parent. The elements below a parent are all those whose numbers lie between its own.



child.left_count > parent.left_count AND child.right_count < parent.right_count

Yes. A depth-first walk arrives at every element below the parent after arriving at the parent and leaves it before leaving the parent. The join must also match exp_id_fk, since each experiment numbers its own tree.



child.left_count < parent.left_count AND child.right_count > parent.right_count

This finds the elements whose numbers enclose the parent’s: the elements above it, not below.



No condition on the numbers will do; a subtree needs a recursive query

A recursive query is needed when only the parent column is kept. The nested set numbers are what let a simple self-join find a subtree.



Check Show answer Reset



2. Which statements about the KSL’s output schema ksl_db are true? Select every one that is.
Select all that apply.



within_rep_stat has a row per response per replication

Yes. Each row holds one response’s statistics in one replication of one run.



A counter, such as LotsCompleted, is kept in within_rep_counter_stat, not in within_rep_stat

Yes. A counter has only its final value in each replication, so the KSL keeps it in a table of its own. within_rep_view combines the two.



A query that joins within_rep_stat to model_element must match the experiment as well as the element

Yes. The key of model_element is the pair (exp_id_fk, element_id), and a statistic stores only element_id_fk. The database does not check that the element exists.



A join of model_element on its parent column alone finds every element below a given element

The parent column gives only direct children. Any depth takes the nested set numbers or a recursive query.



Deleting an experiment leaves its simulation runs in place, to be deleted separately

An experiment owns its runs and model elements, and the KSL’s foreign keys cascade: deleting the experiment deletes everything it produced.



Check Show answer Reset



3. An analyst wants a confidence interval for the frame line’s mean time in shop. Which values serve as the independent observations?



Every lot’s time in shop, from all 30 replications pooled into one list

Lots in the same replication share its congestion: a bad month makes every lot in it slow. Pooling them treats related values as independent and makes the interval too narrow.



The 30 replication averages, one per replication

Yes. Each replication uses different random numbers, so the replication averages are independent observations of the same quantity, and the interval is built from them.



The 5 replications shown first, since the others repeat them

Every replication used different random numbers; none repeats another. All 30 are observations.



The minimum and maximum of each replication

These describe the spread within one replication. The mean is estimated from the replication averages.

1. An engineer reruns an experiment with 120 replications instead of 30, and the replication averages vary about as much as before. About how does the half-width of the 95 percent confidence interval change?



It falls to about half

Yes. The half-width divides the standard deviation by the square root of the number of replications, and four times as many replications halve that factor. The t quantile also falls a little with more degrees of freedom.



It falls to about a quarter

The number of replications enters through its square root, so four times as many replications halve the half-width rather than quarter it.



It stays about the same, since the standard deviation does not change

The standard deviation stays about the same, but it is divided by the square root of a larger number.



It doubles, since there are more values to vary

More replications make the estimate of the mean more precise, never less.



Check Show answer Reset



2. In pw_diff_within_rep_view, experiment A is the one recorded later, ThreeWelders, and a_minus_b is its value less the value of TwoWelders. The average of a_minus_b for TimeInShop is negative. What does the sign say?



Lots spend less time in the shop, on average, with three welders

Yes. A negative difference means A’s values are the smaller: ThreeWelders has the shorter mean time in shop.



Lots spend more time in the shop with three welders

That would be a positive difference, A larger than B.



The view subtracted in the wrong order, so the result must be negated

The order is fixed by which experiment was recorded later. Knowing it, the sign reads directly.



The comparison failed, since a difference of times cannot be negative

A difference is negative whenever the first value is the smaller.



Check Show answer Reset



3. Where does the KSL keep the average, the standard deviation, and the half-width of each response over all the replications of a run?



In across_rep_stat, written as the run finishes

Yes. A row holds the summary of one response over the replications of one run.



In within_rep_stat

That table holds one response’s statistics in one replication, the values a summary is computed from.



In experiment

The experiment table records how the experiment was set up and run, not its results.



Nowhere; the KSL keeps only the replication values, and every summary must be computed in SQL

The KSL stores its summaries. SQL computes the summaries it did not store, and checks the ones it did.



Check Show answer Reset



4. Before trusting a paired comparison from pw_diff_within_rep_view, which checks are worth making? Select every one that is.
Select all that apply.



The count of pairs equals the number of replications in each experiment

Yes. The view pairs rows by rep_id and needs equal replication counts. An experiment with a different count drops out silently, and the summary returns a count of 0 and a NULL average instead of an error.



The stream option columns of ksl_db.experiment are compared for the two experiments

Yes. No single column records whether the experiments shared random numbers, so these columns, and how the experiments were run, are the evidence.



The two experiments’ averages agree to three decimals

If they agreed, there would be nothing to compare. Agreement of the averages says nothing about whether the pairing is sound.



Nothing: the view refuses to pair experiments that did not use common random numbers

The view pairs any two experiments with equal replication counts, whether or not they shared random numbers.

1. Which statements about moving results between long and wide tables are true? Select every one that is.
Select all that apply.



GROUP BY on the observation, with one FILTER per variable, turns a long table wide

Yes. Each group holds one row per variable, and each FILTER keeps the one value that belongs in its column.



One SELECT per variable, combined with UNION ALL, turns a wide table long

Yes. Each SELECT names its variable as a constant and returns its column as the value.



UNION is safer than UNION ALL for making a table long, since it removes duplicate rows

The SELECTs name different variables, so they cannot produce the same row twice. UNION would only spend work looking for duplicates.



In a long table a missing value is an absent row; in a wide table it is a NULL in its row

Yes. The two shapes record the same gap in different ways.



Turning a table wide adds information that the long table did not hold

The two shapes hold the same facts. Every cell of the wide table is one row of the long table.

2. A study stores its results long: one row per replication and variable, with one column naming the variable and one value column. What does this shape give up, compared with a wide table?



A type and constraints of its own for each variable, such as a CHECK that suits only that variable

Yes. A long table has one value column, so every variable shares its one type and whatever constraints the column has.



One summary of every variable with a single GROUP BY

That is the long shape’s strength: grouping on the variable’s name summarizes them all at once.



Any way to tell which replication a value belongs to

Each row of a long table names its observation as well as its variable.



Some of the values, which do not fit in rows

The two shapes hold the same facts; every cell of a wide table is one row of a long one.

3. In the data class SolverRun, bestObjective is a Double and gap a Double?. What does the CREATE TABLE statement the KSL generates from the class make of them?



bestObjective is NOT NULL, and gap may be NULL

Yes. A column is NOT NULL wherever the property’s Kotlin type does not allow null.



Both may be NULL, since a quick table declares no constraints

The KSL maps a type that does not allow null to a NOT NULL column.



Both are NOT NULL, since every column of a quick table is required

The type of gap, Double?, allows null, and so does its column.



gap is left out of the table, since its default value is null

Every var property becomes a column, whatever its default.

An analysis often needs a summary the KSL did not store

The KSL can split a long experiment into chunks run separately, each a simulation run

Each replication is a simulation run of its own

Runs record the random number stream options, which experiments do not

The model is correct on the day it is written and wrong after the next engineering change

The model runs more slowly than one that reads the database

The KSL refuses a model whose times are not read from a database

1. A tool crib keeps one flat table, with a row for each checkout: the tool’s number and description, the employee who took it, and the date. A new torque wrench arrives, and nobody has checked it out yet. Which anomaly keeps the crib from recording the new wrench and its description?



An update anomaly

Nothing is being changed. The trouble is a fact that has no row to go on.



A deletion anomaly

A deletion anomaly loses a fact when a row is removed. Nothing is being removed.



An insertion anomaly

Yes. The wrench’s description can be recorded only on a checkout row, so it cannot be recorded until an unrelated fact, a checkout, exists.



None; the crib can add a row with the employee and the date left empty

A checkout row with no checkout records something that did not happen. The table has no place for a tool on its own, which is the anomaly.



Check Show answer Reset



2. The sales department keeps its orders in the flat order report, a row for each order line with the customer’s number and name and the product’s number and description. Which of these situations are symptoms of the report’s design? Select every one that is.
Select all that apply.



One customer number appears with two different names

Yes. Two names for one number is the trace of a rename that missed some rows: an update anomaly that has already happened.



Deleting a product’s only order line removes every trace of the product’s description

Yes. The description was stored only on that line, so removing the line removes the fact: a deletion anomaly.



A product that has never been ordered cannot appear in the report

Yes. The product’s description needs an order line to sit on: an insertion anomaly.



One order has two lines for the same product

This is legitimate data, not an anomaly. An order may list a product on two lines, and each line is a fact of its own.



Check Show answer Reset



3. Step 4 of the normalization procedure names a table’s normal form. How is it done?



Count the repeated values in the sample rows; the fewer there are, the higher the form

The sample shows where facts repeat, but the normal form is a condition on the dependencies, not a count of values.



Test the table against the normal forms from the first up, and find the first one it fails

Yes. The forms are nested, so the first one a table fails tells you which kind of repeated fact it holds, and which split step 5 must make.



Start from the highest normal form and stop at the first one the table passes

The procedure tests from the first form up, since each form includes the ones below it.



Look up the table’s normal form in the database’s catalog

A database does not know a table’s dependencies, so it cannot name the table’s normal form.

Which functional dependencies do these rows refute? Select every one.
Select all that apply.



tool_number → description

Each tool number appears with one description here, so the rows do not refute it.



description → tool_number

Yes. “Torque wrench” appears with T-1 and with T-2, two values of the dependent for one value of the determinant. Reading a dependency backwards is a common mistake: two tools may share a description.



tool_number → bin

T-1 appears twice, both times in B4, so the rows agree with the dependency.

Yes. “Torque wrench” appears with B4 and with B7.

2. A sales clerk has kept a flat order table by hand for years. A query groups it by customer_number and keeps the groups with COUNT(DISTINCT customer_name) > 1, and it returns three customer numbers. What does that result show?



That customer_number → customer_name is not a rule of the business, and should be dropped from the design

The business still gives each customer one name. The rows broke the rule; they did not repeal it.



That update anomalies have already happened: three customers each carry two or more names

Yes. A dependency is broken wherever one value of its determinant appears with two values of its dependent. In a table kept by hand, this query is the quickest way to find the damage.



That the three customers share a name with some other customer

That would be one name with several numbers, the dependency read backwards. The query found one number with several names.



Nothing, since rows can never say anything about a dependency

Each of the three numbers appears with more than one name, which is exactly what the dependency forbids.

3. A hypothetical table records the steps of work orders: (work_order_number, step_number, work_center, center_manager, hours), with key (work_order_number, step_number). The rules are that each step of a work order is performed in one work center, and each work center has one manager. How does center_manager depend on the key?



Partially, since it depends on part of the key

A partial dependency leaves one column of a composite key. Here the work center depends on the whole key, since a work order has several steps in different centers.



Transitively, through work_center, a column that is not part of a key

Yes. The key decides the work center, and the work center decides its manager. The manager is repeated on every step performed in the center.



Directly on the whole key, so the table has no problem

The manager is decided by the work center alone, whatever the work order or the step.



It does not depend on the key at all

It does, through the chain from the key to the work center to the manager.

1. A query builds a report with one row per order and a column products that holds the order’s product numbers joined into one string, such as “HT-100, GC-300”. Why does such a column belong in a report and never in a stored table?



Because PostgreSQL cannot store a string that contains commas

A text column holds commas like any other character. The trouble is what the value means, not how it is typed.



Because the column holds a list, not a value: a query must search inside strings to find an order of one product, and no foreign key can refer from one element of the list to product

Yes. A list in one cell breaks first normal form. Read in a report, it is convenient; stored, it hides facts the database cannot reach.



Because the report has too few rows to be a table

The number of rows has nothing to do with a normal form.



Because STRING_AGG is PostgreSQL’s own function

The standard’s aggregate, LISTAGG, builds the same list, and the list would be just as wrong in a stored table.



Check Show answer Reset



2. In a functional dependency diagram, order_number and line_number together decide product_number. How is that drawn?



An arrow from each of the two ovals to product_number

Two separate arrows would say that each column alone decides the product, which is false: every order has a line 1.



A larger outline around the two ovals, with the arrow leaving the outline

Yes. Only the two columns together decide the value, so the arrow starts from the outline that holds them both.



One oval holding both names, with no arrow

Each column keeps its own oval, and every dependency is drawn as an arrow.



An arrow from product_number back to each of the two columns

Arrows run from the determinant to the columns it decides, not the other way.



Check Show answer Reset



3. The chapter states BCNF with candidate keys, and adds that, strictly, a determinant may also be a superkey. What is a superkey?



A key made of more than three columns

The number of columns does not make a superkey.



A set of columns that contains a candidate key

Yes. A candidate key with columns added to it still decides every column, so it is a superkey. The book states the rule with candidate keys because a determinant is taken to be as small as it can be.



The primary key, as opposed to the alternate keys

The primary key is the candidate key chosen to identify rows. A superkey need not be chosen at all.



A key that spans two tables

A key belongs to one table. A superkey is a set of a table’s own columns.

1. A hypothetical lot table (lot_number, part_number, part_description, quantity_made) has key lot_number and fails third normal form through part_number → part_description. Which split repairs it?



A new table (part_number, part_description) keyed by part_number, and the lot table keeps part_number but loses part_description

Yes. The determinant and the column it decides move to a new table keyed by the determinant, and the determinant stays behind as a foreign key that refers to it.



A new table (part_number, part_description), and the lot table loses both columns

With part_number gone, nothing says which part a lot made, and joining the two tables cannot give the lots back.



A new table (part_number, part_description) keyed by part_description

The new table’s key is the determinant of the dependency, part_number. Two parts may share a description.



A new table of parts, with part_description kept in the lot table as well, for convenience

Keeping the description in the lot table keeps the repeated fact and the transitive dependency the split was meant to remove.

2. The order report is decomposed into customer, customer_order, order_line, and product, and the dependencies are drawn with each table in its own outline. What in the drawing shows that each table is in Boyce-Codd normal form?



Each outline holds the same number of columns

The tables have different numbers of columns, and the count says nothing about the dependencies.



In every outline, the arrows leave the key and nothing else

Yes. A table whose only determinant is its key meets the condition of BCNF.



No arrow is drawn at all

Every table still has its dependencies. What changed is where the arrows start.



Every column is shaded as part of a key

Most columns, such as customer_name and quantity, are not part of a key, and need not be.



Check Show answer Reset



3. After the order report is decomposed, the transitive chain order_number → customer_number → customer_name is cut at its middle column. What is customer_number in the result?



A column of customer only, removed from the order’s table

With customer_number gone from the order’s table, nothing would say which customer placed an order.



A foreign key in the order’s table, and the key of customer

Yes. The middle column of each chain becomes a foreign key in one table and the key of another, which is how the tables join back together.



A column repeated in every table, so that any two can be joined

It appears only where it is needed: as the key of customer and as the reference to it.



A surrogate key that normalization adds

Normalization works with the natural columns. Surrogate keys are added by the mapping, not by the decomposition.

4. The inspection sheet was normalized under the rule that a lot is inspected once. Suppose instead that a failed lot may be reworked and inspected again. What changes?



lot_number no longer determines the inspector, so the keys of the inspection and of its measurements need the inspection’s time as well

Yes. The dependencies came from a business rule, and when the rule changes, they change. The book’s database anticipates this by giving each inspection its own surrogate key.



Nothing, since the dependencies are found from the rows already recorded

The rule of the business has changed, and the dependencies follow the rule.



The measurement table falls to first normal form

First normal form concerns atomic values, which a second inspection does not change.



The second inspection must be given a new lot number

That would record something false about the lot. The design must change to fit the rule, not the other way round.

1. A class model gives the class OrderLine an attribute orderDate. Which normal form does the mapped order_line table fail?



First normal form

The order date is one value per row, so it is atomic.



Second normal form

Yes. The date depends on the order alone, part of the line’s key, so it is repeated on every line of the order. The repair belongs in the model: the attribute describes the whole, CustomerOrder, not its part.



Third normal form only

Third normal form concerns a column that depends on another column outside the key. The date depends on part of the key.



None; the date describes the line

Every line of an order has the order’s date, so the date describes the order, not the line.

2. Which statements agree with the chapter? Select every one.
Select all that apply.



A report such as the flat order report can be produced by a query or a view when it is needed, while its facts stay stored once

Yes. Normalization governs the tables that store facts, not every table a database shows.



Denormalization is a decision made about a normalized design, and the designer should be able to say which dependencies it gives up

Yes. A designer may store a repeated fact on purpose, to make reading faster or simpler, and accept the anomalies it brings.



A report that people read often must be stored as a table of its own

A query produces the report whenever it is needed, so its facts can stay stored once.



A normal form violation in a mapped table is best repaired in the tables alone, leaving the class model as it was

The violation points to a mistake in the model, and the repair belongs there, so that the model and the tables agree.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 7 Self-Checks
section: Multivalued Dependencies and Fourth Normal Form
text:
Multivalued Dependencies and Fourth Normal Form
Read the section

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. A hypothetical table holds each machine’s certified operators and its maintenance tasks, a row for each combination. The multivalued dependency machine →→ operator holds. Which part of that statement goes beyond a machine simply having many operators?



That each operator is certified on at least one machine

That is a rule about operators, and the dependency does not state it.



That a machine has more than one operator

Many operators per machine is only a one-to-many relationship. A multivalued dependency says something more.



That the set of operators of a machine is the same whatever task the row holds

Yes. Because the set does not depend on the task, every operator must be paired with every task, which is where the repetition comes from.



That the operator determines the machine

The arrow runs from the machine. An operator may be certified on several machines.



Check Show answer Reset



2. The table is split into machine_operator (machine, operator) and machine_task (machine, task). The two join on machine, which is a key of neither. Why is the split lossless all the same?



Because every split into two tables is lossless

Whether a split loses nothing depends on the dependencies behind it, so it must be shown for each split.



Because machine is the primary key of the original table

The original table’s key is all three columns together.



Because every operator of a machine performs every task of the machine, so each pairing the join makes is a row the original table held

Yes. A split on a multivalued dependency is lossless for this reason, not by the rule that governs a split on a functional dependency.



Because the join is written with DISTINCT

DISTINCT removes duplicate rows. It cannot remove a row that was never true.



Check Show answer Reset

title: Chapter 7 Self-Checks
text:
Review of the Whole Chapter
Read the chapter summary

Self-CheckClear all answers


1. One engineer normalizes HG Industries’ flat order report. Another maps the class model of customers, orders, order lines, and products to tables. How do their designs compare?



They differ, since normalization works from data and mapping works from a diagram

The two start from different places and meet at the same design, because both follow the same dependencies.



They have the same four tables and the same dependencies; the mapped database adds surrogate keys and columns the report did not carry

Yes. Normalizing a table that exists and mapping a sound class model are two routes to one design, and a normal form violation in a mapped table points back to a mistake in the model.



Normalization produces more tables, one for each dependency, including one for each column

Each split follows a dependency that breaks a normal form, and the order report needs three splits, giving four tables.



The mapped tables still need normalizing, since a class model ignores dependencies

A class whose attributes each describe its own object maps to tables already in Boyce-Codd normal form.



Check Show answer Reset



2. Which statements agree with the chapter? Select every one.
Select all that apply.



A normal form is a condition on a table’s dependencies that rules out one kind of repeated fact

Yes. Each form names one kind of repetition and the dependencies that cause it.



A key is a smallest set of columns that determines every other column of the table

Yes. A larger set that also determines every column is not a key, since a smaller one does the work.



Fifth normal form concerns tables that can be rebuilt only by joining three or more smaller tables, which is rare in practice

Yes. The book names it and goes no further.



A functional dependency is drawn with an arrow that runs from the column decided to the column that decides it

The arrow runs from the determinant to each column it determines.



Normalization requires each stored table to have a surrogate key

Normalization works with the natural columns. Surrogate keys are a decision of the mapping.



Check Show answer Reset



3. The quality engineers like reading their inspection results as one sheet, a row per measurement with the part’s description and the inspector’s name. How should the database serve them?



Store the sheet as one table, and train the engineers to change every copy of a fact

Every copy is a place where the table can contradict itself, and an insertion or deletion anomaly cannot be avoided by care.



Store the facts in normalized tables, and produce the sheet with a query, or name that query as a view

Yes. The sheet is a fine way to read the results, and a query produces it on demand while each fact stays stored once.



Store both the sheet and the normalized tables, and copy changes from one to the other

Two stored copies are two places to update, the problem normalization removes.



Store each column in a table of its own

Splitting is done on a dependency, not on every column, and a split that drops the key from a table loses the link between its facts.



Check Show answer Reset
